gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.
'Would you like …?' is the standard polite offer.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a supervisor present when students use the lab.
Tomorrow is a public holiday, so we ___ answer any emails.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' shows the action is not necessary: needn't answer.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to see that exhibition before it closes — it is outstanding.
gaps.hint: a strong recommendation with ought to
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' recommends something strongly: ought to see.

gaps.sentence: It is the only blue house on the street, so you ___ miss it.
gaps.explanation: 'You can't miss it' is an idiom meaning it is impossible not to find: can't.
